sentences.text:
This is an application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 [CrPC] seeking anticipatory bail in FIR No.38/2017 dated 20.02.2017 under Sections 279/337/420/468/471 IPC registered at PS: Tilak Marg, Delhi.

2. As per the FIR, on 20.02.2017 at around 12:30 PM, when the complainant was driving his car on Tilak Marg and he stopped at Bhagwan Dass Road Crossing, his car was hit by another car bearing number UP32EN7517, which was being driven by the applicant herein, injuring the complainant and also causing damage to the car of the complainant.
3. During the course of investigation, the vehicles involved in the accident were seized through seizure memo and were deposited in the This is a digitally signed order.

The applicant herein was arrested and granted police bail and was asked to produce his driving licence and the insurance documents of the offending vehicle.
On verification, the said documents were found to be forged.
Thus, though the FIR was initially registered under Sections 279/337, charges under Sections 420/468/471 were added.
Further, proceedings under Section 82 of the Cr.P.C. are also pending against the applicant.
4. Vide order dated 17.03.2023 passed by this Court, the applicant was granted interim protection qua arrest, subject to him joining and cooperating in the investigation.

In terms of the said order,
the applicant joined the investigation on 07.07.2023.

sentences.text: He further submits that the offence as alleged, are bailable in nature, and that Sections 420/468/471 have been arbitrarily added.
He submits that the applicant was merely driving the vehicle and does not own the vehicle.
He further submits that the Driver's Licence and the Insurance documents were also made by the owner of the vehicle and that the applicant had no way to know that the same were forged.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that Section 82 proceedings have only been initiated against the applicant but he has not been declared a 'proclaimed offender'.
He further submits that the applicant is a poor person coming from Bihar and has clean antecedents.
He lastly submits that pursuant to the interim protection granted by this Court, the applicant has since joined investigation.
He thus submits that bail be granted to the applicant as his custodial interrogation is no more This is a digitally signed order.

7. Notice was issued and Status Report was called for.
8. Learned APP for the State, relying upon the Status Report, opposes grant of bail to the applicant in view of the nature and gravity of the offence alleged against the applicant.

Learned APP for the State submits that the applicant herein had not joined investigation despite issuance of notice under Section 41A CrPC and that proceedings under Section 82 CrPC are also pending against him.
He further submits that the custodial interrogation of the applicant is necessary to ascertain the source of the fake and forged documents.
He lastly submits that since the applicant is a permanent resident of Bihar, there is every possibility that he may jump bail.
He thus submits that since the investigation is at a nascent stage, bail be not granted to the applicant.
9. This Court has heard learned counsel for the applicant and the learned APP for the State and gone through the relevant documents on record.

10. The facts involved emanate from an accident between two vehicles, one of which was, though,
driven by the applicant but he was not the owner thereof.
Interestingly, there is neither any averment qua the owner of the vehicle nor has he been made an accused in the present FIR.
Not only that, the car driven by the applicant herein has since been released on 'superdari' to the owner as well.
Under the said circumstances, no malice can be attributed to the applicant.

11. Further, facts disclose that the applicant has joined investigation way back on 07.07.2023 and has been participating therein as and when called for after he was granted interim protection by the learned Trial

As of now, in the considered opinion of this Court, custodial interrogation of the applicant is Ram Kumar vs State on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45425337/
2 no more required.
Seeing the same, it is highly likely that it shall be taking a long period for the trial to get over.
Even otherwise, the applicant is a young man with no prior involvement or antecedents of any kind.
12. Holistically seen, this seems to be a fit case for grant anticipatory bail to the applicant at this stage as the broad parameters for grant thereof are met with.
This is primarily more so whence this Court is not required to critically analyse the evidence on record at the stage of considering grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.
13. Accordingly, the applicant is granted anticipatory bail in FIR No.38/2017 dated 20.02.2017 under Sections 279/337/420/468/471 IPC registered at PS: Tilak Marg, Delhi.

In the event of his arrest, the applicant be released, after furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/-
(Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) alongwith one surety of the like amount by a family member/ friend having no criminal case pending against them, subject to the satisfaction of the learned Trial Court,
and further subject to the following conditions:
i.
Applicant shall ordinarily reside at the address as per the Trial Court records.
If he so wishes to change his residential address, he shall immediately intimate about the same to the I.O. by way of an affidavit.
ii. Applicant shall surrender his Passport to the I.O., within three days.
If he does not possess the same, he shall file an affidavit before the I.O. to that effect within the stipulated time.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 20/12/2023 at 01:09:53 iii.
Applicant shall appear before the Court as and when the matter is taken up for hearing.
iv. Applicant shall join investigation as and when called by the I.O. concerned.
He shall not obstruct or hamper with the police investigation and shall not play mischief with the evidence collected or yet to be collected by the Police.

v. Applicant shall provide all his mobile numbers to the I.O. concerned which shall be kept in working condition at all times and shall not switch off or change the mobile number without prior intimation to the I.O. concerned.
The mobile location be kept on at all times.
vi. Applicant shall report to Police Station Tilak Marg, Delhi once every month in the first week of the month unless leave of every such absence is obtained from the learned Trial Court.

vii. Applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity and shall not communicate with or come in contact with any of the prosecution witnesses, the victims or any member of the victim's family or tamper with the evidence of the case or try to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police Ram Kumar vs State on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45425337/
3 officials.
14.
Accordingly, the present application is allowed and disposed of in the aforesaid terms.
15. Copy of this order be sent to the concerned S.H.O. for necessary information and compliance thereof.
